1.note: The pronoun **her** refers to the people of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **distress**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [distressing things came]
The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh dishonored]
The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will glorify]

2.note: Isaiah is speaking as if the people’s distress and suffering were **darkness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The people who are suffering greatly]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **darkness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in dark places]

Isaiah is speaking as if deliverance and hope were **a great light**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will experience great deliverance]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **deep darkness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a land where darkness is very deep]

2.q: הָ⁠עָם֙ הַ⁠הֹלְכִ֣ים בַּ⁠חֹ֔שֶׁךְ רָא֖וּ א֣וֹר גָּד֑וֹל יֹשְׁבֵי֙ בְּ⁠אֶ֣רֶץ צַלְמָ֔וֶת א֖וֹר נָגַ֥הּ עֲלֵי⁠הֶֽם
2.note: These two sentences **The people walking in darkness will see a great light** and **The dwellers of a land of deep darkness, light will shine on them** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [The people walking in darkness will see a great light. Indeed, for the dwellers of a land of deep darkness, light will shine on them]

3.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you will make them more joyful]
The pronoun **it** refers to the nation. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the nation of Israel]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the rejoicing at the harvest** is a time of great gladness and celebration, so is the joy that the people will experience before Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as joyful as people are at the harvest]

The point of this comparison is that just as **they exult when they divide spoil** because they celebrate a victory, so the people will celebrate the deliverance that Yahweh brings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as they celebrate a great victory]

4.q: כִּ֣י אֶת־עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗⁠וֹ וְ⁠אֵת֙ מַטֵּ֣ה שִׁכְמ֔⁠וֹ שֵׁ֖בֶט הַ⁠נֹּגֵ֣שׂ בּ֑⁠וֹ
4.note: The pronouns **his** and **him** refer to the people of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. See the UST.

Isaiah is speaking as if the oppression the people endured were **the yoke of his burden**, a wooden frame placed on an animal to make it carry a heavy load. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the burden he forced them to carry]

Isaiah is speaking as if the oppression were **the staff of his shoulder**, a rod used to beat someone on the shoulder. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the rod that beat him on his shoulder]

Isaiah is speaking as if the oppression were **the rod of the one oppressing him**, an instrument used to beat him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the one oppressing him with harsh treatment]

The point of this comparison is that just as God defeated the Midianites decisively in the time of Gideon, so he will defeat the oppressors of his people now. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [just as you defeated Midian]

5.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because]

Isaiah says **every boot of one booting in commotion** as an overstatement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [every last boot of every soldier marching in the tumult]

Isaiah is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [every boot worn by a soldier marching]

The expression **the garment rolled in blood** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the garment that blood had soaked]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **burning**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [burned]

6.note: The expression **a child has been born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God has given a child]

The expression **a son has been given** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God has given a son]

Isaiah is speaking as if authority and rule were a physical burden that could be placed on someone’s shoulder. He says **the dominion will be on his shoulder** to express that the child will bear responsibility for ruling. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the child will bear responsibility for ruling]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **dominion**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [authority to rule]
The pronoun **one** refers to people in general. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And people will call his name]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **Wonder** that is characterized by **a Counselor**, that is, a counselor who is wonderful. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a Counselor who is wonderful]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **Prince** that is characterized by **Peace**, that is, a ruler who brings peace. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a ruler who brings peace]

7.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 9:6.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and people being at peace]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **no** and the negative word **end**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [there will be abundance]

Here, **the throne of David** represents the royal authority that David held. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [ruling with the authority that David had]

Here, **to establish it and to sustain it** marks **with justice and with righteousness** as the goal or purpose of ruling **on the throne of David and over his kingdom**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. See the UST.

The terms **justice** and **righteousness** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [by ruling fairly]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with fair judgments]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and with right actions]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **zeal**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [The deeply committed]

8.note: Isaiah is using the phrase **The Lord has sent a word** to introduce a new section about judgment against Israel. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Isaiah is speaking as if Yahweh’s message of judgment were a physical object that he **sent** like a projectile. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [has declared a message of judgment against Jacob]

Here, **Jacob** represents the people of the nation descended from the patriarch Jacob. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Jacob]

Isaiah is speaking as if Yahweh’s word were a physical object that **has fallen on** Israel. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it has come true for Israel]
The pronoun **it** refers to the word that the Lord sent. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [that word has fallen]

Here, **Israel** represents the people of the nation descended from the patriarch Jacob. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

9.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **pride**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [proud hearts]

Isaiah is using **greatness of heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “arrogance.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and in great arrogance]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **greatness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how proud they were]

10.q: לְבֵנִ֥ים נָפָ֖לוּ וְ⁠גָזִ֣ית נִבְנֶ֑ה שִׁקְמִ֣ים גֻּדָּ֔עוּ וַ⁠אֲרָזִ֖ים נַחֲלִֽיף
10.note: The people actually mean to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what they are saying here. They are boasting that they will rebuild better than before, but in reality they are defying God’s judgment. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [When our enemies cause destruction, we will rebuild even better than before]

The expression **Sycamores have been cut down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the sycamores have come down]

11.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because Yahweh has raised up]

The standard written Hebrew text as we have it today reads “the adversaries of Rezin.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “the princes of Rezin.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

The pronouns **him** and **his** refer not to Rezin but back to Israel in verse 8. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [against Israel, and he has spurred on Israel’s enemies]
Here the pronoun **his** refers to Israel, not to Rezin. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [he has spurred on the enemies attacking Israel]

12.note: Isaiah is speaking as if the military conquest of Israel were an animal that **devoured** its prey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they completely conquered Israel]
The pronoun **they** refers to Aram and the Philistines. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [these enemies have devoured]

Isaiah is using **his nose has not turned back** as a common expression of the culture to mean “his anger has not subsided.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his anger has not subsided]

12.q: בְּ⁠כָל־פֶּ֑ה בְּ⁠כָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠ע֖וֹד יָד֥⁠וֹ נְטוּיָֽה
12.note: This is poetic language. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here.

Here, **his hand** represents Yahweh’s power and readiness to act. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and he is still ready to punish]
The pronoun **his** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s nose … Yahweh’s hand]

13.note: The pronoun **the one striking it** refers to Yahweh as the one who is punishing the people. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, who struck them]

13.q: וְ⁠הָ⁠עָ֥ם לֹא־שָׁ֖ב עַד־הַ⁠מַּכֵּ֑⁠הוּ וְ⁠אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ
13.note: The pronoun **it** refers to the people as a collective, while the pronoun **they** refers to the individual members of the people. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people has not returned to the one striking the group of people, and the individual people have not sought Yahweh of Armies]

14.note: The word translated as **So** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, Yahweh will cut off]

Isaiah is speaking of the important people in Israel as if they were the **head** of an animal and as if they were a majestic **palm branch** high in the air. He s speaking of the less important people in Israel as if they were the **tail** of an animal and as if they were a lowly **reed** in a marsh or on a river bank. Your language may have comparable expressions that you can use in your translation. You could express these images as comparisons, as the UST does.

Isaiah is referring to all of the people in Israel by describing two major types, wealthy or important people and poorer or less important people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the people]

Isaiah is referring to all of the classes of people in Israel by naming two major components, **palm branch** and **reed**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the great and the lowly]

15.note: Isaiah is using **the lifted of face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “a person who is honored or respected.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and those who are honored]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **falsehood**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [false things]

16.note: Isaiah is speaking as if the leaders were **guides** leading people along a path, but they are leading them in the wrong direction. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For the leaders of this people are causing them to go in the wrong direction]

Isaiah is speaking as if these **guided ones** were **being swallowed up**, as if they were food being consumed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and its guided ones are being destroyed]

The expressions **guided** and **being swallowed up** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express these ideas in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and this destroys the ones they guide]

Isaiah is using the adjective **guided** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. The ULT adds the term **ones** to show that. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those who are being guided by them] or [those whom they are guiding]

17.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result]

The pronoun **its** refers to the people or nation of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people’s young men … the people’s orphans … the people’s widows]

Isaiah is using **every mouth** to represent the people who are speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and every person is speaking foolishness]

Isaiah says **all of it is godless and doing evil** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [nearly everyone is godless and doing evil]
The pronoun **it** refers to the people or nation of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [all of Israel is godless]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **foolishness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [foolish things]

18.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **fire** spreads rapidly and destroys everything in its path, so **wickedness** spreads and destroys the society which hosts it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like fire, wickedness burns and spreads rapidly, destroying everything in its path]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wickedness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [doing wicked deeds]

Isaiah is speaking of **wickedness** as if it were a living thing that could **devour** whatever is around it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it consumes the briars and the thorns]

Isaiah is speaking of **wickedness** as if it were a living thing that could **kindle** a fire. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And fire kindles in the thickets of the forest]

19.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wrath**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [By the wrathful aspect of]

The expression **the land is scorched** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has scorched the land]

Isaiah is speaking as if divine judgment were fire that **scorched** the land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the land is ruined]

The point of this comparison is that just as **fuel of fire** is consumed and destroyed by flames, so the people will be consumed by God’s judgment. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [the people are like fuel that the fire consumes]

20.note: The pronoun **he** refers to each person or man. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And each man will cut off … but he will be hungry, and he will eat]
The pronoun **they** refers to the people in general. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people will not have enough]

Isaiah is speaking as if self-destruction and civil conflict were a man eating **the flesh of his arm**, consuming his own body. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a man will destroy himself]

21.note: Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Manasseh will attack Ephraim; and Ephraim will attack Manasseh]
See how you translated the similar expression in 9:12.
